title: Two nests, both at their largest — can you see either one?
question: In either picture, can you see anything that reads as a nest — rooms, galleries, worked ground? Or is this just dirt to you?
context_md:
**The lab bed, seed 3, frame 120,000 — the frame where each nest is biggest** (roofed void is still climbing at the end in both, so neither has peaked and collapsed). Cropped to the colony: the nest site is at x=256, dead centre, and the view spans 120 columns around it at 8x. Zoom out one step for the margin.

The two arms differ by **one switch**: whether the crowding-driven chamber-digging urge is on. Same bed, same seed, one binary.

**What I measured, and why I am asking rather than telling.** By the counters, B has **1.8x the roofed room** of A — that is the result I was about to report to you as 'the chamber mechanism is making chambers worse'. But B also dug **3.7x as much** and has **4x the open hole**, so per dig it is worse at making rooms, and you have already told me once that a big hole is not a structure.

**And I could not see a nest in either picture.** Not at this zoom and not at 2x. If that is what you see too, then the honest finding is not 'A vs B' at all — it is that several hundred cells of chamber are invisible in play, which no counter would ever have told me. The burrow probe measured why once: a tunnel interior is the only thing in the bed with no colour of its own, against soil whose brightness spans 119 of 255.

Ignore the plants and the lamps; the question is the ground.
